solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Making another appearance in theatre?

parts.note: surface sense: returning to the stage; cryptic sense: being given a new face or look
surface sense: on stage; cryptic sense: in the operating theatre of a hospital

explanation.surface: An actor seems to be making a comeback on the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre is the operating theatre, and the new appearance is literal: a reshaped face or body.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic operations alter a patient's looks, so the patient comes out with a different appearance after the surgeon's work.

clue.text: Disorder in pros far worse — they can't fight any more

indicators.note: used as a verb: put these words into disorder, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Professionals have got far worse at something, and chaos results.
explanation.definitionFit: Captured soldiers are held in camps until hostilities end, so they are out of the fighting.

clue.text: Hold up article, in turn, as circus performer

indicators.note: the hold-up and the article are placed in the turn

parts.note: a turn is a stage act or performance
to hold up is to rob at gunpoint

explanation.surface: Something about stopping an article and performing at the circus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' looks like a reversal signal; here it is a performer's act.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbler doing flips and balancing feats is a classic big-top entertainer.

clue.text: Its mercurial rise may indicate need for care

definitions.text: Its mercurial rise may indicate need for care

parts.note: surface sense: someone's sudden volatile rise in fortune; cryptic sense: a column of mercury climbing
a high reading signals fever, so the patient needs nursing

explanation.walkthrough: Mercurial suggests a temperamental person; here it is literally mercury rising in a glass tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinical instrument measures body temperature, and a high reading shows a fever needing treatment.

clue.text: Hot food repeatedly found, from what we hear, in cold country

indicators.text: repeatedly found, from what we hear
indicators.note: the answer is heard twice over: once as a word for cold and again as the name of a South American country

parts.note: cold weather is chilly

explanation.surface: Spicy dishes keep turning up even in a frosty land.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sounds like both chilly (cold) and Chile (the country), hence 'repeatedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: This pepper, or the spicy stew made with it, is the standard example of fiery cooking.

clue.text: Life put in disarray, with daughter being given raise

indicators.note: letters put in disarray are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A life thrown into chaos, but at least a daughter has received a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' sounds like a salary increase; here it means lifted up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lifted or elevated, physically or in spirits, has been hoisted higher.

clue.text: CO, for example, leads in generating appropriate strategy

indicators.note: the leads of a group of words are their opening letters, so each word gives its first

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A commanding officer leads in devising a suitable plan.
explanation.walkthrough: CO looks like Commanding Officer; it is the chemical formula for carbon monoxide.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon monoxide is a colourless poisonous vapour, one instance of this state of matter.

clue.text: What lies behind pupil swallowing second drink

indicators.note: the eye part takes the letter for second inside it

parts.note: the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye

explanation.surface: A schoolboy downing a second glass of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupil' looks like a schoolchild; it is the eye's opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek resinated white wine is a well-known alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Reckon English king liberal — that disproves hypothesis

parts.note: to reckon is to count up
Rex is Latin for king, as in royal signatures
liberal in the sense of generous or plentiful

explanation.surface: A sceptic weighs up an English liberal monarch who disproves a theory.
explanation.definitionFit: A single case that breaks a general claim is enough to refute that claim in logic.

clue.text: Serial broadcast before or after one from part of Middle East

indicators.note: the letter for one may go either before or after the rearranged word; both give the answer
something broadcast is scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A radio serial airs before or after another programme from the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually the rearrangement works with the I at either end.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for something originating in the Jewish state on the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Host mangled and consumed by lion in African enclave

indicators.note: the jumbled word is eaten up inside the lion

parts.note: Leo is the lion of the zodiac

indicators.note: mangled letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A host is mauled and eaten by a lion somewhere in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: This mountain kingdom lies entirely surrounded by South Africa, a country within another country.

clue.text: Gold braid, initially part of royal regalia

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: only the initial letter of the next word is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Golden braid forms part of the crown jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: The sovereign's jewelled globe is carried at a coronation among the crown jewels.

clue.text: Bad behaviour in stag party, in part

parts.note: a stag is a male deer
a faction is a part or splinter group of a political party

explanation.surface: Some misbehaviour went on at a stag do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stag party' looks like one phrase; it splits into a male and a party faction.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrongdoing or evil conduct, an old word related to malefactor, a criminal.

clue.text: Company run right notices changes and amendments

indicators.note: used as a verb: the word changes its letter order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A firm publishes notices of changes and amendments.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the cricket abbreviation for run.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixes made to a text or document are synonymous with revisions to it.

clue.text: Note altered by doctor put in grave situation

indicators.note: altered letters are changed into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor changes a note, landing someone in serious trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave situation' reads as a crisis but means a burial place.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury a body in a tomb or vault is a synonym for interring it.

clue.text: Go from nine to five, say, as covered by official order

definitions.text: Go from nine to five, say

indicators.note: the small word is wrapped inside the order

parts.note: a decree is a formal edict
taken as written

explanation.surface: Office hours, nine to five, set by official decree.
explanation.walkthrough: Nine to five suggests working hours; it is a number getting smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling in value from nine down to five is an example of lessening, so the verb fits.

clue.text: Fellers from west of England having hewn elms in error

indicators.note: letters placed in error are mixed up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Woodcutters from the West Country chopped down elm trees by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellers' suggests tree-fellers; it means fellows. Wales lies west of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of Wales are men from the country bordering England on its western side.

clue.text: Locate said bishop's office to get views on holiday

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the word for locate sounds like a word for view

parts.note: to site something is to locate it
a see is a bishop's seat or diocese

explanation.surface: Instructions for finding a bishop's office to enjoy the scenery while away.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourists visit famous attractions to look at them, the typical holiday pastime.

clue.text: Journey top-class — secure fare from Hungary

parts.note: to journey is to go
U means upper-class in British usage
to lash is to tie down securely

explanation.surface: Travel first class and lock in the fare for a trip to Hungary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests a ticket price; it is food.
explanation.definitionFit: This paprika-seasoned meat stew is Hungary's national dish.

clue.text: European beer knocked back in feast

indicators.note: the drink is turned backwards, as if downed in one

parts.note: lager is a pale beer

explanation.surface: A continental drinker downing lager at a banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' looks like drinking; it turns the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain lavishly with food and drink, as a verb meaning to treat guests.

clue.text: Part of crustacean or insect upset queen

parts.note: the ant is a common insect

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: Queen Anne, the last Stuart monarch

explanation.surface: A lobster or bug has annoyed royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or insect' seems part of the definition; the insect is in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeler on the head of a crab or lobster is a sensory appendage.

clue.text: Inadequate? Some agree, but not all

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are taken, from within them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A partial consensus is a rather thin result.
explanation.definitionFit: A meagre portion is scanty or insufficient in amount.

clue.text: Giving off glow and awful fouler smell

indicators.note: awfully arranged letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: Something glowing and giving off a dreadful stink.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluorescent materials emit visible light when struck by radiation, so they shine.

clue.text: Something for elevenses? It's not quite eleven

indicators.note: the side lacks its final letter

parts.note: a football or cricket side has eleven players

explanation.surface: A morning cuppa arrives a touch before eleven o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Elevenses is a British mid-morning snack; 'eleven' is not the time but a team.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup of the hot brew is the traditional British mid-morning refreshment.

clue.text: Characters reassembled in an ending for film outside Indian city

indicators.note: these letters wrap around the city name

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is used

parts.note: the word whose final letter is taken
Agra is the city of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: A film ends with scenes shot around an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the very device crossword solvers know best: letters rearranged into a new word.
explanation.definitionFit: A word made by rearranging the letters of another is exactly characters put back together differently.

clue.text: Argument in bank? Heard otherwise

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a quarrel, rhyming with cow
second meaning: a line or tier, as of seats, rhyming with toe

explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard otherwise' tells you the two meanings are pronounced differently though spelt the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling covers a noisy quarrel and a line of things arranged side by side.

clue.text: Adult opponents holding hands in circle

indicators.note: the opponents are placed in the circle

parts.note: a circle of friends is a group
in bridge West and North sit as opponents, each holding a hand of cards

explanation.surface: Rivals clasp hands in a ring, like children at play.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players are named by compass points; West and North are on opposing sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A mature person who has reached full age is no longer a child.

clue.text: After one season, uninspired play

indicators.note: the word for uninspired comes after the season

parts.note: the winter is one of the four seasons
stale means flat and lacking freshness

explanation.surface: A season has passed, leaving someone dull and jaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's late romance featuring Leontes and the famous bear exit is a stage drama.
